text.p: British soft drinks and chocolate group Cadbury Schweppes Plc Wednesday posted a 2 percent gain in half-year profits to 236 million pounds ($383.4 million) and said it had a good start to its second half.
The company makes about 60 percent of its profits in the second half of the year as confectionery sales surge in winter and at Christmas.

Beverage sales in the United States, where it owns the Dr Pepper/7UP brands, make up some 60 percent of Cadbury-Schweppes total drinks sales and drink sales in the region contribute about 35 percent of total group profits.

Operating profits from its beverages division rose by 29 percent to 198 million pounds ($322 million) in the six months to June 14, while the confectionery division achieved a 3 percent rise to 105 million ($171 million).

However, the strength of sterling on foreign exchange markets reduced earnings from the beverages division by 11 million pounds ($18 million) and by five million ($8 million) for the confectionery division.
The company's results were released overnight on the Australian Stock Exchange, where it is also listed, by its local offshoot, Cadbury Schweppes Australia Ltd.
Revenues from continuing operations fell to 1.837 billion pounds ($2.99 billion) from 1.894 billion ($3.08 billion), a rise of 5 percent on a constant currency basis.

Cadbury, which sold its 51 percent stake in Coca-Cola Schweppes Beverages Ltd in June for 623 million pounds ($1.01 million), has more room for acquisitions, Chief Executive John Sunderland said. The sale of the group's CCSB interest cut borrowings by 45 percent to 882 million ($1.4 billion) at the half-year stage and led to a pre-tax gain of 417 million ($678 million).

In North America, where there have been worries over the ability of Cadbury's Dr Pepper/7UP subsidiary to compete with the might of Coca-Cola and PepsiCo, Sunderland said the group has managed to slow the rate of 7UP's sales decline.

"We have slowed the rate of decline. It was going down by about 4 percent per annum pretty steadily and we have bought that back to 2 and the trend is actually stabilising. The core 7UP brand has actually grown. We have chosen to support the key brand and that is paying off gradually, but I don't want to be over optimistic," Sunderland said.

In the six months, Dr Pepper sales rose 4.3 percent, out-growing overall soft drinks market growth of 3 percent. The United States accounts for about 40 percent of soft drinks sold world-wide. Some 60 percent of soft drinks consumed in the Americas are colas.
